scope: seams.7 WebSocket lifecycle correction. Local acceptance passes; Linux build and Clippy pass; timed Google active-claim qualification remains pending.

facts.fact: The workerd barrier control reads both claims as running. Releasing the held second reply completes the pair and an independent wallet.
The first Google trial observes running claims, then SIGKILL, takeover epoch 2, burned state and refusal without another connection. Signal timing was not bounded before the 15-second timeout.
That Google trial logs shutdown_handoff_stalled despite exit code 0. Its raw passed status does not qualify successful drain.
A local two-node active-claim kill completes within 284 ms and drains when it omits the later independent-wallet request.
Adding the independent wallet after takeover reproduces the stalled YaoConnectionProxy response-body pin on seams.6. The local SIGKILL upper bound is 421 ms.
The same local Wallet reproduction passes and drains on the seams.7 candidate, including the independent wallet after takeover.
The final four-case fixture fails on seams.6 when a remote socket is registered as local; celld panics because the object is not resident.
The same fixture passes on the clean seams.7 build: local owner, remote owner, remote relay, rejected upgrade, and clean shutdown.

causes.cause: A WebSocket response retains an HTTP-body activity.
causes.assessment: Supported by the response_body drain pin, local full-Wallet reproduction, and removal of that pin after the runtime discards the upgrade body stream.

causes.cause: A forwarded remote target is registered in the caller node ownership core.
causes.assessment: Supported by the nonresident-object panic. Skipping local registration for tunneled targets removes the failure in the same fixture.

causes.cause: Wallet protocol or cryptographic changes are required.
causes.assessment: Contradicted for these failures: the same Worker package bytes pass after runtime-only corrections.

causes.cause: The initial Google trial proves active execution at the actual signal.
causes.assessment: Not established. The timed driver now requires the complete execute-to-confirmed-SIGKILL interval below 15 seconds.

classificationScope: Runtime compatibility defects. Wallet application and cryptographic code are unchanged.
changes: Keep upgrade validation, but register only locally owned accepted sockets in the local core.
Release the HTTP-body activity when transferring a WebSocket response.
Release a rejected parked tunnel and reuse the existing owned upgrade/splice path for peer relays.
Fail Google qualification when shutdown logs a stalled handoff, even if the process exits 0.
limits: Simple local echo already drained on seams.6; it did not reproduce the body-pin failure. The full post-takeover Wallet scenario did.
Ordinary /state snapshots omit drainPins. Their absence is not evidence of zero active pins.
The workerd reference covers echo and rejected-upgrade behavior in one runtime, without distributed or drain parity claims.
The raw initial Google and local diagnostic status fields are overridden by the stated timing and shutdown limits; they are not successful qualification records.
The corrected Google timing/drain scenario has not yet run on seams.7.
Peer partitions, distributed relocation, Google restore/provider-failure cases, upgrade/rollback with active claims, and release promotion remain open.
Current package evidence refers to the frozen 0.11.0 candidates before the next dev rebase; newer registration optimizations require refreshed candidates.

review.scope: Independent source and diagnostic review identified the timing gap, false-positive drain result, tunneled-target cleanup, and forwarded relay path. Final Google qualification remains open.

productionLatency: No new Wallet request, database call, network round trip, or blocking validation. The runtime removes invalid ownership tracking and response-body retention.
